clue.text: Crowded public transport by day's end

parts.note: a bus is a common form of public transport

indicators.note: end points to the final letter of the word day's, before the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Buses get packed at the close of the working day.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowded street or shop is a busy one; the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Went out, taking in clubs to get intoxicated

indicators.note: taking in says the first piece swallows the second, holding it inside

parts.note: to go out of a room is to exit, so went out gives exited
C is the card-playing abbreviation for clubs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' suggests nightclubs or golf, but it is the card suit, abbreviated C.
explanation.definitionFit: Intoxicated can mean thrilled or exhilarated as well as drunk, which is the sense of being worked up.

clue.text: University wise men, local, somewhat dull

parts.note: the Magi were the wise men who visited the infant Jesus
a native of a place is a local

explanation.surface: Academics and local people at a university are described as rather boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking imagination makes work or people flat and uninspiring, which is a mild kind of dullness.

clue.text: Fish hard to hold in creels

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the word creels

explanation.surface: An angler finds a slippery catch difficult to keep in the basket.
explanation.walkthrough: A creel is an angler's wicker basket, which fits the fishing picture.
explanation.definitionFit: This long fish is notoriously slippery and wriggly, hence the phrase about being slippery as one.

clue.text: Antelope seen in Eastern country

parts.note: a land is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A grazing animal spotted in some nation of the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal named is a large African antelope with spiralled horns, a specific example of the type.

clue.text: Bad conjunction of ice and gale is rather sad

explanation.definitionFit: Elegies are mournful poems, so anything in their mood is plaintive and melancholy.

explanation.surface: Liverpool Football Club leads the league when its players are on form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liverpool' invites football, but here it is the city on the Mersey, a major shipping harbour; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is a coastal city with large docks, an example of a harbour town for ships.

clue.text: Start to ask for money at home

parts.note: to beg is to ask for money or charity
someone in is at home

explanation.definitionFit: Start and the answer are straightforward verb synonyms for commencing something.

clue.text: Trouble with radon being uncovered

indicators.note: being uncovered means the outer letters of radon are stripped away, leaving the inside

explanation.definitionFit: The answer means fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Test area for French wine with good soil

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so for
vin is the French word for wine
ground is earth or soil

explanation.surface: A vineyard trial plot where French grapes are grown in fine earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where weapons, vehicles or ideas are tried out is a testing site, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: An ideal partner with strength to capture Myrrha's heart

indicators.note: to capture means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: might is power or strength

indicators.note: heart picks out the central letters of the name Myrrha

explanation.surface: A strong suitor wins the heart of a woman named Myrrha.
explanation.walkthrough: Myrrha has six letters, so its heart is the central pair, not a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names the perfect man someone hopes to marry, the one who is exactly suitable.

clue.text: Joker adds finish to puzzle for regular income

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit

indicators.note: finish to points to the final letter of the word puzzle

explanation.walkthrough: Joker is also this puzzle's setter, which makes the surface a sly self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay received at fixed intervals for work is a synonym for steady earnings.

clue.text: Capital needs less urbanisation on reflection

indicators.note: reflection, as in a mirror, says the hidden letters are read backwards
on reads as sitting upon the words, the letters lying across needs less urbanisation

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave no hidden-word signal; 'on' supplies it, with 'reflection' as the reversal. 'On reflection' reads as reconsidering, hiding both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgium's seat of government, and home of the EU institutions, is an example of a capital city.

clue.text: Cut of game bird, but not the tail

indicators.note: but not the tail says the last letter of the bird is dropped

parts.note: the snipe is a wading bird shot as game

explanation.surface: A butcher's portion of shot bird, served without its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut made with scissors; both words work as noun or verb.

clue.text: Like things good to eat? Be dealing with deli

indicators.note: dealing, as cards are shuffled and dealt, signals that these letters are mixed up

explanation.definitionFit: The answer is an adjective describing anything safe or fit to be consumed as food.

clue.text: One applauding heads of company making filming equipment

the board of directors are those at the top of a company

explanation.definitionFit: This hinged slate is snapped shut at the start of each take to synchronise picture and sound.

clue.text: Town's leader being successful in linking with another one

explanation.definitionFit: Town pairing is a formal link between two places, so joining with another counterpart fits.

clue.text: Sketched river in the morning dampness

parts.note: dew is the moisture found on grass early in the day

explanation.definitionFit: Sketched is a past-tense synonym for having drawn a picture.

clue.text: Trying to impress pending pro-am arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts these letters into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: A pro-am is a golf event pairing professionals with amateurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Casually mentioning famous acquaintances is a well-known way of showing off to others.

clue.text: A mammal in flight raised public disturbance in slaughterhouse

parts.note: the bat is the only mammal that truly flies

parts.note: a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is the plain English term for the building where animals are killed for meat.

clue.text: Spoon most of cat food made with pasta

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
a noodle is a strip of pasta

explanation.definitionFit: To spoon is a dated term for courting affectionately, a synonym for kissing and cuddling.

clue.text: Time anything at all is imparted in school

parts.note: aught is an old word meaning anything

explanation.surface: Any knowledge whatsoever gets handed on in the classroom eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers pass on knowledge, so lessons imparted in a classroom were instructed to pupils.

clue.text: Unwanted e-mails? Well, maybe at first

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word maybe

explanation.surface: Someone muses over whether some messages in their inbox are junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a filler word, but it is a spring of water.

clue.text: Brazil, perhaps, turned up a fish good to eat

indicators.note: turned up means the word is read upwards in this down entry, so backwards

parts.note: a Brazil is an example of a nut

explanation.surface: Brazil, the country, turned out to offer a tasty seafood catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil' suggests the country, but here it is a Brazil nut.
explanation.definitionFit: This large ocean fish is widely eaten, fresh or tinned, so it is an example of an edible fish.
